name: Code Editor
tagline: Edit JSON, XML and other code in a multiline text column, with Monaco.
summary:
Replaces the plain text box on a multi-line text column with Monaco, the editor from VS Code, for solutions that keep JSON or XML in a column and need somebody to edit it safely.

- Syntax colouring for fourteen languages, with bracket matching, folding, and find and replace
- Strict validation for JSON, XML and FetchXML, with every fault marked and named
- Checking, completion and hover from a JSON Schema kept as a web resource
- FetchXML completion with your environment's own tables, columns and choices
- **Format** for JSON, XML and FetchXML
- **Changes**: what you changed since the record was saved, side by side, and still editable
- A **Markdown preview**, sanitised, with images only from your own environment
- A **JSON tree** to browse a document by keyboard or mouse, copy a node's path, and jump back to its text

Monaco is compiled into the solution, so nothing is fetched at runtime. In a canvas app, `isValid` can gate a Save button; on a form the editor shows a fault but cannot refuse a save. The other languages are coloured, not checked.

presets.name: JSON, light
presets.description: A JSON document with validation on and a Format button in the strip beneath the editor.

presets.name: Two faults
presets.description: A trailing comma and a comment: the first is named in the strip, both are marked in the editor, and Format still tidies what parses.

presets.name: Against a JSON Schema
presets.description: Well-formed JSON that breaks its schema five ways — a type, a minimum, a missing property, an enum and an extra property — each marked and worded. On a form the schema is a web resource; here it is passed inline, as a canvas app would.

presets.name: JSON, as a tree
presets.description: The order opened as a read-only tree. Arrows move and open nodes, Enter goes back to the node’s text in the editor, Ctrl+C copies its path, and the strip shows what the schema says about the node in focus.

presets.name: Suggestions from the schema
presets.description: An order with room for more. Type a quote on the empty line — or after the colon of a key — and the schema offers what fits there, required properties first; rest the pointer on a property to read its description. Enter takes a suggestion.

presets.name: Dark, fit to content
presets.description: Forced dark theme, and the editor sized to its document up to 400px rather than a fixed box.

presets.name: XML
presets.description: An XML document; well-formedness is checked by the browser's own parser.

presets.name: FetchXML
presets.description: A FetchXML query: type < under the entity, or a space inside a tag, for what goes there. The misspelt element is a fault. On a form your tables, columns and joins come too; the demo has no environment to read them from.

props.code:
<fetch top="5">
  <entity name="account">
    <attribute name="name" />
    <atribute name="accountnumber" />
    <filter type="and">
      <condition attribute="createdon" operator="last-x-days" value="7" />
    </filter>
    
  </entity>
</fetch>

presets.name: Markdown, rendered
presets.description: A checklist kept as Markdown and opened rendered (Open Markdown in: Preview). Images come only from the environment itself; one from another site is a link, never fetched. Edit in the strip switches to the text.

props.code:
# Release checklist

Kept in a **multiline text column**, written in Markdown. Press **Edit** in the strip to change it, **Preview** to read it again.

- [x] Bump the version
- [ ] Write the release notes
- [ ] Tag with `npm run release`

| Step | Who |
|------|-----|
| Pack | CI |
| Publish | You |

> A bare tag publishes one compare link, so annotate it.

```
git tag -a --cleanup=verbatim v1.6.0 -F .release-notes.md
```

An image from another site is never loaded, only linked: ![a tracking pixel](https://example.com/pixel.png)

<details><summary>Safe HTML</summary>Basic tags such as <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> and <sub>sub</sub> survive; scripts, styles, frames and media do not.</details>

presets.name: Markdown, as text
presets.description: The same checklist opened as text, as every Markdown column did before 1.6.0. Type a line, and Changes appears in the strip: the document against what was saved, side by side where there is room.

limitations: The schema is passed inline here; on a model-driven form it is a web resource, which the demo has none of. The isValid and problemCount outputs are reported but nothing in the demo consumes them.

FetchXML: your tables, columns, joins and choice values come from an environment’s table definitions, which the demo has none of, so only FetchXML’s own elements, attributes and operators are offered and checked here.

Markdown: on a form, images from your own environment are drawn; the demo has no environment, so only inline data: images are, and a link opens nothing here. Changes compares with the preset’s text, because the demo never saves.
